title: Booksellers fear their rarest books are being pulped to feed AI. The trail leads to a ‘recycler’.
excerpt: Australian booksellers fear rare titles are being pulped to train AI, after odd bulk orders from a Canadian book ‘recycler’. Anthropic and Zoom Books deny it.
content_html:
We have written about why AI companies are buying up old books: printed before the internet filled with machine-made text, they are a clean source of language, free of AI slop. This is what that hunger looks like from the other end. In Australia, secondhand booksellers fear someone is slicing apart and pulping the rarest titles on their shelves to train the machines.

The fear traces to a US copyright case against Anthropic, brought by book authors. Unsealed files revealed a practice called “destructive scanning”: buy the book, slice off the spine, scan the pages, pulp the rest. The Washington Post reported the company tried to keep it quiet. A judge ruled it lawful, as “transformative use.”

The practice is now understood to be widespread, with 404 Media reporting that intermediaries have stepped in to feed it. That is where Australia’s booksellers come in. Several noticed strange waves of orders through the big secondhand marketplaces, Abebooks and Biblio, and started asking who was buying.

The buyer, in many cases, was a Canadian “book recycler” called Zoom Books. As the Guardian reported, the orders were price-insensitive and oddly random. Delfina Manor, in Victoria, got three boxes in May and asked them to stop. One order paired a 1970s soil-mechanics manual with a $9 poetry book that had sat unsold for 20 years.

‘More than just objects’

For sellers drowning in stock, the sales are not all bad. Nick Dawes, who keeps about 500,000 books with his wife Jenny, would happily sell in bulk. His line is the irreplaceable one. “If somebody said to me, look, this is the only known copy, I’m going to cut it up, then I’d say, I think I’d rather not send it to you.”

Tim White of Books for Cooks draws the same line. A $20 book with half a million copies in Australia, he would not mourn. A one-off, “it’s horrific.” AI is not the first buyer to destroy books for profit; dealers have long sliced rare volumes to sell the illustration plates. As bookseller Gwenyth Todd puts it, “to me books are more than just objects.”

Two denials, one silence

Both companies named in the story deny the worst of it. An Anthropic spokesperson said it has never bought from Zoom Books, that it sources books from mainstream commercial markets, and that “none of our data acquisition programs buy and destroy rare or antiquarian books.” Buying books to train models, it added, is common across the industry.

Zoom Books, whose co-founder said on LinkedIn it had been “expanding aggressively,” says it resells books intact and does not digitise them, recycling only what cannot be rehomed. It would not say whether it sells intact books on to AI firms for scanning. Its commercial agreements, it said, require confidentiality.

That silence is the problem. No vendor has proof their books were destroyed, and the concern is the opacity, not a proven act. A bookseller can screen a buyer they can see. They cannot screen a supply chain that ends behind a confidentiality clause. For a common paperback, no great loss. For the only surviving copy of something, there is no undo.

content_html_zh:
我们已经写过为什么人工智能公司正在购买旧书：在互联网出现之前印刷的充满了机器文本，它们是干净的语言来源，没有人工智能的污点。 这就是饥饿从另一端看起来的样子。 在澳大利亚，二手书商担心有人将书架上最稀有的书籍切成碎片并打成浆来训练机器。

这种恐惧可以追溯到美国针对 Anthropic 的版权诉讼，该诉讼由书籍作者提起。 未密封的文件揭示了一种被称为“破坏性扫描”的做法：购买这本书，切掉书脊，扫描页面，将其余部分打成浆。 据《华盛顿邮报》报道，该公司试图保持沉默。 法官裁定其合法，为“变革性用途”。

据了解，这种做法现在很普遍，据 404 Media 报道，中介机构已介入助长这种做法。 这就是澳大利亚书商发挥作用的地方。 一些人注意到大型二手市场 Abebooks 和 Biblio 上出现了奇怪的订单浪潮，并开始询问谁在购买。

在许多情况下，买家是一家名为 Zoom Books 的加拿大“图书回收商”。 据《卫报》报道，这些订单对价格不敏感，而且随机性奇怪。 维多利亚州的德尔菲娜庄园（Delfina Manor）在五月份收到了三个盒子，并要求他们停止。 其中一份订单将一本 20 世纪 70 年代的土壤力学手册与一本 9 美元的诗集配对，这本诗集已经滞销了 20 年。

“不仅仅是物体”

对于库存过剩的卖家来说，销售情况也不全是糟糕的。 尼克·道斯 (Nick Dawes) 和妻子珍妮 (Jenny) 收藏了大约 50 万本书，他很乐意批量出售。 他的路线是无可替代的。 “如果有人对我说，看，这是唯一已知的副本，我要把它剪掉，然后我会说，我想我宁愿不把它寄给你。”

《厨师书籍》的蒂姆·怀特也提出了同样的观点。 一本售价 20 美元、在澳大利亚拥有 50 万册的书，他不会哀悼。 一次性的，“这太可怕了。” AI并不是第一个为了盈利而销毁书籍的买家；经销商长期以来一直将稀有卷切开来出售插图板。 正如书商格温妮丝·托德 (Gwenyth Todd) 所说，“对我来说，书籍不仅仅是物品。”

两次否认，一次沉默

报道中提到的两家公司都否认了最糟糕的情况。 Anthropic 的一位发言人表示，它从未从 Zoom Books 购买过书籍，而是从主流商业市场采购书籍，并且“我们的数据采集程序都不会购买和销毁稀有或古籍书籍。” 它补充说，购买书籍来训练模型在整个行业都很常见。

Zoom Books 的联合创始人在 LinkedIn 上表示，该公司一直在“积极扩张”，并称该公司转售原封不动的书籍，并不将其数字化，只回收那些无法重新安置的书籍。 它没有透露是否将完整的书籍出售给人工智能公司进行扫描。 该公司表示，其商业协议需要保密。

这种沉默就是问题所在。 没有供应商能够证明他们的书籍被销毁，人们担心的是不透明性，而不是经过证实的行为。 书商可以筛选他们能看到的买家。 他们无法筛选以保密条款为终点的供应链。 对于一本普通的平装本来说，并没有太大的损失。 对于某物的唯一幸存副本，无法撤消。
